# Mixed Models with an Extra Zero Part

`MixedModel` in **glmmadaptive** is designed to support zero-inflated and
two-part mixed effects models via the `zi_fixed` and `zi_random` arguments
and the corresponding `family` objects.  For both model types the user
specifies the fixed- (and optionally random-) effects formula for the
logistic regression that governs the zero part.

## Current implementation status

> **Note:** Zero-inflated and hurdle families are **not yet implemented** in
> the Python port.  The classes listed below exist as stubs — they expose the
> correct attributes (`has_zi`, `family`, `link`, `n_phis`) but raise
> `NotImplementedError` for every computational method.  Attempting to
> construct a `MixedModel` with any of these families will raise
> `NotImplementedError`.  Full implementations will be available in a future
> release.

| Family (R) | Python class | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `zi.poisson()` | `ZIPoisson` | Stub — not yet implemented |
| `zi.negative.binomial()` | `ZINegativeBinomial` | Stub — not yet implemented |
| `zi.binomial()` | `ZIBinomial` | Stub — not yet implemented |
| `hurdle.lognormal()` | `HurdleLogNormal` | Stub — not yet implemented |
| `hurdle.poisson()` | `HurdlePoisson` | Stub — not yet implemented |
| `hurdle.negative.binomial()` | `HurdleNegativeBinomial` | Stub — not yet implemented |

```{python}
from glmmadaptive.families import (
    ZIPoisson, ZINegativeBinomial,
    HurdlePoisson, HurdleNegativeBinomial, HurdleLogNormal,
)

# All stubs declare the correct metadata:
for cls in [ZIPoisson, ZINegativeBinomial, HurdlePoisson,
            HurdleNegativeBinomial, HurdleLogNormal]:
    fam = cls()
    print(f"{cls.__name__:30s}  has_zi={fam.has_zi}  link={fam.link}  n_phis={fam.n_phis}")
```

The R equivalents and the expected Python API (once implemented) are shown
in each section below.

---

## Zero-Inflated Poisson Mixed Effects Model

The zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) model uses a logistic regression to model
the probability of a structural zero, and a Poisson distribution for the
non-zero counts.  In the R package this is fitted with `family = zi.poisson()`
and the extra arguments `zi_fixed` and (optionally) `zi_random`:

```r
# R code (not yet available in Python)
fm1 <- mixed_model(
    y ~ sex * time,
    random   = ~ 1 | id,
    data     = DF,
    family   = zi.poisson(),
    zi_fixed = ~ sex
)

# Extend with a random intercept in the zero part (correlated with count RE)
fm2 <- update(fm1, zi_random = ~ 1 | id)

# Likelihood ratio test
anova(fm1, fm2)
```

The expected Python API (future release):

```python
# Python API (planned — raises NotImplementedError currently)
from glmmadaptive import MixedModel
from glmmadaptive.families import ZIPoisson

fm1 = MixedModel(
    fixed    = "y ~ sex * time",
    random   = "~ 1 | id",
    data     = DF,
    family   = ZIPoisson(),
    zi_fixed = "~ sex",
).fit()

fm2 = MixedModel(
    fixed     = "y ~ sex * time",
    random    = "~ 1 | id",
    data      = DF,
    family    = ZIPoisson(),
    zi_fixed  = "~ sex",
    zi_random = "~ 1 | id",
).fit()

from glmmadaptive.results import MixModResults
print(MixModResults.anova(fm1, fm2))
```

## Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Mixed Effects Model

The zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model extends ZIP by adding an
over-dispersion parameter $\theta = \exp(\phi)$ to the non-zero part.  In
R it is fitted by substituting `zi.negative.binomial()` for `zi.poisson()`:

```r
# R code (not yet available in Python)
gm1 <- mixed_model(
    y ~ sex * time,
    random   = ~ 1 | id,
    data     = DF,
    family   = zi.negative.binomial(),
    zi_fixed = ~ sex
)

# Non-nested comparison with ZIP + ZI random effect
anova(gm1, fm2, test = FALSE)
```

Expected Python API:

```python
# Python API (planned)
from glmmadaptive.families import ZINegativeBinomial

gm1 = MixedModel(
    fixed    = "y ~ sex * time",
    random   = "~ 1 | id",
    data     = DF,
    family   = ZINegativeBinomial(),
    zi_fixed = "~ sex",
).fit()
```

## Two-Part Mixed Effects Model for Semi-Continuous Data (HurdleLogNormal)

The hurdle log-normal family models continuous data with excess zeros.  A
logistic regression governs the zero/non-zero split; a linear mixed model
with log-normal errors governs the positive part.  The estimated dispersion
parameter `exp(phis)` is the standard deviation of the log-normal errors.

```r
# R code (not yet available in Python)
km1 <- mixed_model(
    y ~ sex * time,
    random   = ~ 1 | id,
    data     = DF,
    family   = hurdle.lognormal(),
    n_phis   = 1,
    zi_fixed = ~ sex
)

# Extend with an uncorrelated random intercept in the zero part
km2 <- update(km1, random = ~ 1 || id, zi_random = ~ 1 | id)

# Marginalised coefficients for (1 - π) × E{log(Y)}
marginal_coefs(km2)
```

Expected Python API:

```python
# Python API (planned)
from glmmadaptive.families import HurdleLogNormal

km1 = MixedModel(
    fixed    = "y ~ sex * time",
    random   = "~ 1 | id",
    data     = DF,
    family   = HurdleLogNormal(),
    zi_fixed = "~ sex",
).fit()
```

## Two-Part / Hurdle Poisson Mixed Effects Model

The hurdle Poisson model uses a logistic regression for the zero/non-zero
split and a zero-truncated Poisson distribution for the positive counts.
The fixed-effects coefficients relate to the mean $\mu$ of the **full**
(untruncated) Poisson distribution, not to the conditional mean given a
positive count.

```r
# R code (not yet available in Python)
dm1 <- mixed_model(
    y ~ sex * time,
    random   = ~ time | id,
    data     = DF,
    family   = hurdle.poisson(),
    zi_fixed = ~ sex
)

dm2 <- update(dm1, zi_random = ~ 1 | id)
anova(dm1, dm2)
```

Expected Python API:

```python
# Python API (planned)
from glmmadaptive.families import HurdlePoisson

dm1 = MixedModel(
    fixed    = "y ~ sex * time",
    random   = "~ time | id",
    data     = DF,
    family   = HurdlePoisson(),
    zi_fixed = "~ sex",
).fit()
```

## Two-Part / Hurdle Negative Binomial Mixed Effects Model

The hurdle negative binomial family is identical in structure to the hurdle
Poisson family, but replaces the zero-truncated Poisson with a zero-truncated
negative binomial distribution, thereby accommodating over-dispersion in the
positive counts.

```r
# R code (not yet available in Python)
hm1 <- mixed_model(
    y ~ sex * time,
    random   = ~ time | id,
    data     = DF,
    family   = hurdle.negative.binomial(),
    zi_fixed = ~ sex
)

hm2 <- update(hm1, zi_random = ~ 1 | id)
anova(hm1, hm2)
```

Expected Python API:

```python
# Python API (planned)
from glmmadaptive.families import HurdleNegativeBinomial

hm1 = MixedModel(
    fixed    = "y ~ sex * time",
    random   = "~ time | id",
    data     = DF,
    family   = HurdleNegativeBinomial(),
    zi_fixed = "~ sex",
).fit()
```
